_comment: DEMO profile (DEMO_READINESS_2026-09-06 rows 5/8). Loaded on top of appsettings.json when DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT=Demo (scripts/StartInterface52.ps1 sets it). Carries what the TEST runner otherwise injects per process for the VR-Forces 5.2d profile (RunC2SimScenario.ps1 AppEnv52), plus the demo-only choices. Env vars (Vrf__X) still override everything here.

Vrf._TypeMappingMode: The 5.2 fidelity table (unit-type-map-52.json: per SIDC function + echelon + side, EXACT/PROXY rows) is read ONLY in FidelityTable mode; the base default RealTemplates is the 5.0.2 parity dispatch (every company = Tank Company (USA), hostile included) - found live on COA-STP1 run 1, 2026-09-06.
Vrf._MakRuntime: In-process runtime bootstrap (MakRuntime.cs): the exe prefixes its PATH with these bin dirs and sets MAK_VRFDIR/MAK_VRLDIR/MAK_RTIDIR, RTI_RID_FILE and RTI_ASSISTANT_DISABLE before the bridge loads. No start script needed; a configured value overrides a differing process variable (logged), empty keys leave the environment alone. `VrfC2SimApp --runtime-check` verifies the install before a demo.
Vrf._ApplicationNumber: DEMO block 9101-9199: outside the test ledger (docs/OPUS_EXECUTION_PLAN.md NEXT FREE, 4xxx) so a demo never collides with a test federate; two interfaces on ONE network must use different numbers.
Vrf._ClientId: MUST equal the SystemName of the init STP pushes (RUNBOOK sec 2). STP's own inits use STP; COA-STP1 uses C2SIM - override with Vrf__ClientId or StartInterface52.ps1 -ClientId.
Vrf._CreationPolicy: C13 (user ruling 2026-09-06): the init is the whole ORBAT (context); only order-referenced units are simulated. AtOrder = every unit is an empty shell at init (displays, reflects its position, sits in the org tree); members are created when an order first references the unit. AtInit = the oracle's create-everything (COA-STP1: 1,300-1,700 objects, the crawl).
Vrf._DeStackCreates: C14 (user ruling 2026-09-07): units that share one coordinate (STP puts a whole COA on its assembly point) are spread onto hex rings at init, 700 m apart - larger than the longest shipped company formation (630 m) so no two units' formations overlap. Confirmed by PREREG_ASSEMBLY_LAYOUT: blocking 63 vs 4,828 messages, the composed company's formation gate opened, first task completions at scale.
Vrf._DeStackComposedSiblings: C14 amended (user ruling 2026-09-21): composed siblings that share a coordinate are spread too - around their parent, which keeps its position, at their own echelon's spacing (platoon 350 m), because D6 measured the parent's formation leaving three platoon aggregates 24-56 m apart with all three footprints overlapping. false restores the 2026-09-20 behaviour for a comparability run.
Vrf._ArrivalApproachFraction: STP-837 amended (user ruling 2026-09-21): a member's traversal bar is its own share of its own approach - max(min(0.5 x route, 0.5 x its distance to the last vertex at dispatch), ArrivalMinTravelMeters) - so a member that starts near the destination can be counted once it has genuinely travelled. 0 restores the route-length bar.
Vrf._TaskPredecessorTimeoutSeconds: A FLOOR under the successor gate, not the whole window (M1, 2026-09-14): since R4 a task whose predecessor carries a C2SIM Duration waits at least that Duration x Vrf:DurationScale plus Vrf:TaskPredecessorEndMarginSeconds, whichever is larger. The harness default (600 s) abandoned 31 of COA-STP1's 42 tasks on 2026-09-07; the 7200 here was the manual answer to that, and it was NOT enough either - the ten tasks gated on a PT2H predecessor lost by a second or two, deterministically, because the completion fires strictly after dispatch + Duration. The derivation is what fixes it; this value is kept as the floor for a predecessor that has NO Duration at all.
Vrf._DispatchReadinessTimeoutSeconds: DEFER, DO NOT ABORT (D5b, 2026-09-21), and the demo profile states it outright because it decides what a demo-day race LOOKS LIKE. A task whose taskee is not taskable yet - the init's creates have not been issued, or its object has not reflected - is HELD for up to this many WALL seconds and then dispatched, instead of being DROPPED/REFUSED the way run 20260921T072530Z_wayb's order was 0.31 s after the init. It also holds an order-time materialization until the init's own creates have settled, so the init's creations and the order's delete/re-creates no longer land on the back end together. The operator's instrument is the READY TO TASK line: wait for it before pushing the order (DEMO_RUNBOOK sec 3/4) and neither wait happens at all. 0 restores the pre-2026-09-21 behaviour. A taskee that is not in the initialization is still refused at once, and a hold ends early when STP-822 declares the back end lost.
Vrf._PlacementReclamp: PLACEMENT RE-CLAMP (2026-09-21), and the demo profile states it outright because a ground unit belongs ON the ground in front of an audience. (CORRECTION 2026-09-21: this text opened 'IT IS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A DEMO AND A STATIONARY VEHICLE' and closed 'rather than shown to an audience sitting still under the ground'. Both fused being off the terrain with not moving. 'Born buried, therefore never moves' is FALSIFIED - docs/VRF_ALTITUDE_FRAMES.md sec 5 and the sec 7 tripwire - and nothing here claims or needs it.) Run 20260921T114910Z is the case: Iron Storm on MAK Earth over a cold Suwalki AO, the init's terrain query unanswered, 36 of 36 objects created at the FALLBACK altitude, and the two single-platform taskees - one of them the registered T14-only fallback cut - measured by the interface itself at live -0.0 m against terrain of 145.4 m and 155.8 m, tasked anyway, and reported COMPLETE. That is the measurement. The design implication, separately: the interface must not task a unit it has itself measured off the ground without saying so, and the justification is the placement contract (UG52 14.3.3), not any claim about what burial does to movement. With this true an object placed on the fallback is re-measured, corrected with the documented setLocation at its own live lat/lon (CORRECTION 2026-09-21: this said 'setAltitude(0 m above ground level)'; the code calls _bridge.SetLocation - VrfC2SimService.cs:3433 and :3559 - and setAltitude is ignored for a non-air vehicle, setAltitudeRequest.h:23-25) and CONFIRMED BY READING ITS ALTITUDE BACK, and a taskee measured more than Vrf:PlacementReclampToleranceMeters off the terrain at dispatch is LOGGED and dispatched. (CORRECTION 2026-09-25, RL-20260921-06: until then it was HELD as [BOUND-BUT-NOT-ON-THE-GROUND] and, if no read-back confirmed the correction, REFUSED with a TASKABRT - in run 20260921T143243Z the read-back never landed and two legitimate tasks were ended. A correction with no read-back is now counted 'corrected, read-back not received', not NEVER MEASURED.) What an operator watches for: the PLACEMENT RE-CLAMP summary line. A DEMO-DAY MITIGATION THAT COSTS NOTHING: pre-warm the AO (load the scenario and let MAK Earth stream) before pushing the init, and the PLACEMENT summary reads 'N of N ... from the TERRAIN QUERY', the re-clamp never arms, and this setting does nothing at all.
Vrf._TimedCompletion: COMPLETION ON START TIME + DURATION - the owner's TEMPORARY position (docs/RULINGS.md RL-20260921-09: 'let's take the temporary position that completion is based on start time + duration ... If they arrive after the expected start time + duration, they complete immediatelly'), implemented 2026-09-25 (scope approved as RL-20260925-01). WHAT THE SETTING DOES, as built since then: a task with a C2SIM Duration ends at dispatch + Duration x Vrf:DurationScale. A unit that arrives (or a VR-Forces task that ends) EARLIER is held and reported TASKCMPLT at that end time. A task WITH a destination whose unit is still travelling at the end time is NOT reported complete then: one OVERDUE line is logged, its follow-on tasks keep waiting, and TASKCMPLT is sent the moment it arrives. A task with NO destination (hold, defend, fire, follow, patrol) ends at its end time. A STUCK unit is reported TASKABRT by the progress watchdog (Vrf:StallDetection, ON in this profile) and its follow-ons are abandoned. Whether a task's desired effect was achieved is ignored. HISTORY, kept because it is why this text changed: from 746c091 (2026-09-14) until 2026-09-25 every task was reported TASKCMPLT at its end time whether or not its unit had arrived, on a reading of the 2026-09-14 answer '4 given by the end time' - a question about SECURE, OCCUPY and DEFEND (RL-20260914-02) - that docs/CORRECTIONS_LOG.md F-1 withdrew. ON is the default in code; it is written here because a demo profile must not keep its most visible choice in C# only: most of COA-STP1 is hold-type work the simulation can never evidence, so with this OFF nothing completes, no STREND successor dispatches, and the demo is nine tasks of the forty-two (run G6).
Vrf._StallDetection: ON IN THE DEMO PROFILE ONLY - the owner's decision of 2026-09-25 (RL-20260925-01); the shipped default in VrfSettings.cs and appsettings.json stays OFF. Since 2026-09-25 the Duration timer no longer ends a task whose unit has not arrived (RL-20260921-09), so this progress watchdog is the ONLY thing that reports a STUCK unit: no member moved more than Vrf:StallMoveMeters over the calibrated window -> one TASKABRT (the code STP sees for a stalled unit, RL-20260914-01), report-only (the task stays in flight and may still complete on a later arrival), and that unit's follow-on tasks abandoned with their own TASKABRTs. With it OFF a stuck unit gets no terminal report at all and its follow-ons wait until Vrf:TaskChainBackstopSeconds.
Vrf._TaskClock: M2 (cold-start review of 5c67d41; Q2, user ruling 2026-09-14). WHICH CLOCK a C2SIM task time is measured on: the Duration that ends a task, the StartTime/DelayTimeAmount delay that holds one back, and the STREND predecessor gate - all three, or the chain breaks. "sim" is the VR-Forces scenario clock with an automatic WALL fallback when it cannot be read AND no back end is present (Q5: while a back end IS present a flat clock is a PAUSE and task time HOLDS). At COA-STP1's measured ratios (0.27x-0.73x) sim and wall differ by a factor of three to four, so this is not a detail. Vrf:StallClock is the progress watchdog's knob and governs nothing here.
Vrf._DurationScale: R4's compression, on the ORDER'S AUTHORED TIME. 1.0 = the order as written, and the only value that reproduces it. A demo that cannot sit through COA-STP1's PT1H20M and PT2H tasks sets this lower - 0.05 turns the whole 42-task graph into minutes - and it scales BOTH halves of the order's clock, the Duration that ends a task AND the StartTime delay that holds one back (T13's 3h20m), so a compressed demo does not still wait three hours for its breach. Validated once at start-up: zero, negative, NaN and the infinities are REJECTED with an ERROR and the run proceeds at 1.0.
Vrf._TaskPredecessorEndMarginSeconds: M1: the slack added to the predecessor's own end time when deriving how long a successor waits for it to COMPLETE. Covers the 1 s timed-walk cadence and the dispatch-then-arm ordering inside MarkDispatched.
Vrf._TaskChainBackstopSeconds: A1 (pass-2 review of 0c96f50): how long a gate waits for its predecessor to DISPATCH AT ALL, when that predecessor is a task in the SAME order. Generous on purpose - a predecessor that really dies is ABANDONED, which fails the gate at once, so a timeout here only ever punished a healthy deep chain. Measured with the old rule, COA-STP1 dispatched 21 of its 42 tasks and TASKABRT'd the other 21 at BOTH the 600 s default and the 7200 above. A DANGLING startAfterTaskUuid still expires at Vrf:TaskPredecessorTimeoutSeconds.
Vrf._SupersededTaskCode: Q1 (user ruling 2026-09-14). VR-Forces runs ONE task per unit, so dispatching a new one REPLACES the running one. TASKABRT at the supersede point is the ruling: the taskee is demonstrably not performing it, and its STREND successors are abandoned with it. TASKCMPLT keeps the old task's armed end time (the literal R4 reading) and is selectable. Not reachable on COA-STP1 under PredecessorTimeoutPolicy=skip - no taskee has two ungated tasks.
Vrf._PreflightRouteShift: USER RULING 2026-09-20: 'Route shift: ON. Use as default for any run.' ON is now the default in code AND in appsettings.json; it is repeated here because the demo profile must state its behaviour-changing choices outright. Evidence: V8b met every pre-registered criterion with the shift and the zero-offset control V8z froze - the LATERAL OFFSET is the remedy. WHAT THE DEMO OWES IT: a PRE-WARMED tile cache for the AO plus Vrf:PreflightOffline=true, or the first dispatch of each ground move waits on HTTP tile fetches up to Vrf:PreflightRouteShiftTimeoutSeconds (30) before falling back to the authored line. Set false here, or Vrf__PreflightRouteShift=false / StartInterface52.ps1 -RouteShift off, to turn it off.
Vrf._PreflightElevationLevel: STP-802. The TMS level the pre-flight samples elevation dataset 149 at, and the FLOOR of its automatic fallback. 13 is the deepest level served over the MOJAVE AO and is what the 0.92 threshold was calibrated on; the DEMO AO is the Suwalki Gap, where dataset 149 returns NO DATA at 13 and serves the ground at 12 (measured 2026-09-20, 0 of 25 grid samples over the SuwalkiN20 box). Both keys are written here because the demo profile must not keep an AO-dependent choice in C# only: leaving the start at 13 with the floor at 11 lets the same build serve either AO, and the interface LOGS which level each area resolved at. A coarser level SMOOTHS the sustained window (40 m spans 4.2 postings N-S at L13, 2.1 at L12), so a real face reads LOWER - the threshold is conservative there, not transferred.
Vrf._PreflightWarnings: Left OFF, stated rather than implied (DEMO_READINESS row 20). OFF means the post-dispatch scoring pass does not run; the route shift above still scores every ground move BEFORE dispatch and still reports what it did, what it declined to do, any leg with no elevation at any level, and any leg crossing water. Turning this on adds a second scoring pass and a second set of ObservationReports for the same legs - useful when the audience should see the pre-flight's own verdicts, not needed for the shift.
